## Proof

We compute the operator norm $\|A\| = \sup_{\|f\|_1 = 1} \|Af\|_1$.

**Upper bound.** For $f \in L^1[1,2]$,

$$\|Af\|_1 = \int_0^1 |Af(x)|\,dx = \int_0^1 \left|\int_1^2 \frac{f(t)}{x+t}\,dt\right|dx \le \int_0^1\int_1^2 \frac{|f(t)|}{x+t}\,dt\,dx.$$

By Tonelli's theorem (integrand nonnegative),

$$\|Af\|_1 \le \int_1^2 |f(t)|\left(\int_0^1 \frac{dx}{x+t}\right)dt = \int_1^2 |f(t)|\,\Big[\ln(x+t)\Big]_{x=0}^{x=1}\,dt = \int_1^2 |f(t)|\,\ln\!\frac{1+t}{t}\,dt.$$

Define $g(t) = \ln\frac{1+t}{t} = \ln(1+t)-\ln t$ on $[1,2]$. Then $g'(t) = \frac{1}{1+t}-\frac{1}{t} = -\frac{1}{t(1+t)} < 0$, so $g$ is strictly decreasing and attains its maximum at $t=1$:

$$g(t) \le g(1) = \ln 2.$$

Therefore $\|Af\|_1 \le (\ln 2)\,\|f\|_1$, giving $\|A\| \le \ln 2$.

**Lower bound (attaining the supremum).** For $n \ge 1$, set $f_n(t) = n\,\mathbf{1}_{[1,\,1+1/n]}(t)$, so $\|f_n\|_1 = 1$. Then

$$\|Af_n\|_1 = \int_0^1\int_1^{1+1/n}\frac{n}{x+t}\,dt\,dx = n\int_0^1\left[\ln\!\left(x+1+\tfrac{1}{n}\right)-\ln(x+1)\right]dx = n\int_0^1 \ln\!\frac{x+1+1/n}{x+1}\,dx.$$

For each $x \in [0,1]$, using $\ln(1+u) \le u$ with $u = \frac{1}{n(x+1)}$,

$$n\ln\!\frac{x+1+1/n}{x+1} = n\ln\!\left(1+\frac{1}{n(x+1)}\right) \le n\cdot\frac{1}{n(x+1)} = \frac{1}{x+1},$$

which is integrable on $[0,1]$. Moreover, as $n\to\infty$,

$$n\ln\!\left(1+\frac{1}{n(x+1)}\right) \to \frac{1}{x+1}.$$

By the dominated convergence theorem,

$$\lim_{n\to\infty}\|Af_n\|_1 = \int_0^1 \frac{dx}{x+1} = \Big[\ln(x+1)\Big]_0^1 = \ln 2.$$

Since $\|f_n\|_1 = 1$ for all $n$, we obtain $\|A\| \ge \lim_{n\to\infty}\|Af_n\|_1 = \ln 2$.

**Conclusion.** Combining both bounds,

$$\boxed{\|A\| = \ln 2.}$$
